replacement.questionText: For the data set 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 the interquartile range is to be found. The convention used here is the EXCLUSIVE convention: the median itself is excluded before the data is split into lower and upper halves. The interquartile range is
replacement.explanation: Split the ordered data and remove the median 5 first: the lower half is 1, 3 so Q1 = (1 + 3) ÷ 2 = 2, and the upper half is 7, 9 so Q3 = (7 + 9) ÷ 2 = 8. IQR = Q3 − Q1 = 8 − 2 = 6. The answer 4 is what the INCLUDE-median convention gives (lower half 1, 3, 5 → Q1 = 3; upper half 5, 7, 9 → Q3 = 7; IQR = 4) — it is only right under a convention this stem does not use. 8 is the full range (9 − 1), not the interquartile range. 3 is the median, which measures the centre rather than the spread.
